# Instructor guide — Building Agents with OpenAI

Copy this into your teaching notes. Times are elapsed teaching time; add breaks separately. Detailed explanations, exercises, and solutions live in [course-guide.md](course-guide.md).

## Before learners arrive

- Read [verification.md](verification.md) and use only the live paths confirmed for this teaching project.
- Run `make setup`, `make rehearse`, and `make test`. Open the deck, two core notebooks, app, and a fallback recording.
- Check signed-in playground controls and managed/model access. Keep the API key on the backend; never project `.env` or classroom token files.
- If a live path fails, switch to the labeled offline rehearsal or a saved capture. Do not troubleshoot credentials on the projector.
- Review token rates if estimating model cost. Unknown prices stay unknown; managed sandbox/tool charges require separate accounting.

## Teaching timeline

- **0:00–0:15 · Setup & map (15 min)**
  - Say: “The model chooses actions; the runtime executes the loop; tools supply capabilities; the application enforces permissions.”
  - Show: `course/config.py`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course preflight` → `uv run python -m course demo --runtime offline --follow-up --output outputs/setup`.
  - Ask learners: Draw four boxes: model, runtime, tool, application. Place choose a function, execute Python, enforce publisher permission, and keep conversation history in the correct boxes.
  - Check: Point to the model setting, the tool dispatcher, the brief schema, and the application permission check. Explain why offline success cannot verify API access.
  - Fallback: Use the offline demo and replay. Teach the distinction between deterministic simulation and captured live output explicitly.

- **0:15–0:35 · Playground: first useful agent (20 min)**
  - Say: “An answer becomes useful when we can show where it came from and what it cannot establish.”
  - Show: `course/prompts.py`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course demo --runtime managed --output outputs/playground-fallback`.
  - Ask learners: Use the first prompt and save the answer. Underline every factual claim and attach its supporting quotation.
  - Check: Show the tool name, its input, and returned evidence. Identify a claim that goes beyond the source, even if the prose sounds confident.
  - Fallback: Run the API-based completed demo. If no live path is available, show the offline result and ask students to audit evidence; do not describe that as a playground run.

- **0:35–1:05 · Managed agent in Python (30 min)**
  - Say: “Configuration is reusable; a session is one continuing piece of work.”
  - Show: `course/runtimes/managed.py`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course demo --runtime managed --follow-up --output outputs/managed` → `uv run python -m course cleanup`.
  - Ask learners: Trace one function request from requires_action to ToolBox.dispatch and back to input.tool_result. Record the two correlation IDs.
  - Check: Find the session creation, stream opening, tool-result submission, completion condition, and cleanup. Explain which state the follow-up reused.
  - Fallback: Replay a labeled capture if available. Otherwise walk through managed.py beside the deterministic offline two-turn demo; mark managed API access unverified.

- **1:05–1:30 · Responses: expose the loop (25 min)**
  - Say: “The model asks for a function; this Python line is what actually runs it.”
  - Show: `notebooks/0.0-intro-responses-api.ipynb`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course extract` → `uv run python -m course demo --runtime responses --follow-up --output outputs/responses`.
  - Ask learners: Open exercise.py. Implement matching_outputs so every model function call receives a JSON-encoded function_call_output with the original call_id.
  - Check: Point to self.tools.dispatch in ResponsesRuntime. Explain why a well-formed JSON result can contain an unsupported claim.
  - Fallback: Run extraction offline and the local exercise solution. Replay a saved Responses run if present; label offline behavior as simulation.

- **1:30–1:55 · Agents SDK: own the runtime (25 min)**
  - Say: “The SDK runs the loop inside our application; our application still owns its permissions and state strategy.”
  - Show: `course/runtimes/sdk.py`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course demo --runtime sdk --follow-up --output outputs/sdk` → `uv run python -m course demo --runtime sdk --failure read_paper --output outputs/sdk-failure`.
  - Ask learners: Choose a runtime for a hosted research worker that should retain progress between tasks. State one reason and one responsibility that remains yours.
  - Check: Find Agent, a function_tool, Runner.run_streamed, and the saved SDK history. Explain what the SDK replaced and what remains application code.
  - Fallback: Inspect sdk.py alongside the offline demo; use local events or a recorded SDK output to compare state. Do not claim Runner ran if the SDK live call was unavailable.

- **1:55–2:15 · Grounding & actions (20 min)**
  - Say: “Evidence can inform the answer. It cannot grant itself permission to act.”
  - Show: `course/actions.py`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course actions` → `uv run python lessons/05-grounding-actions/demo.py --runtime offline`.
  - Ask learners: Open exercise.py and complete the authorization decision table: approval absent, permission absent, wrong owner, changed digest, valid request, repeated valid request.
  - Check: Show that model text cannot publish. Explain why both approval and authorization are required, and why approving one digest cannot authorize an edited brief.
  - Fallback: The mock action and local retrieval demos require no API. Use them to demonstrate the authorization boundary even when live model behavior is unavailable.

- **2:15–2:40 · Evaluate & repair (25 min)**
  - Say: “A trace explains what happened. An evaluation judges whether it met the task.”
  - Show: `evals/cases.json`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course evaluate --runtime offline --output evals/results/classroom-before` → `uv run python lessons/06-evaluate/solution.py`.
  - Ask learners: Open exercise.py. Create a schema-valid brief that cites an exact quotation from the supplied synthetic passage but makes a stronger claim than the quote supports.
  - Check: Show all ten rows, one concrete failure, the repair, and the rerun. Explain what the mechanical scores cannot establish.
  - Fallback: Run the offline suite and inspect its recording. Label it as harness coverage; use saved live results only when their metadata identifies a genuine API run.

- **2:40–3:00 · Ship & recap (20 min)**
  - Say: “The interface can request work; the authenticated backend decides whose work it is and what may happen.”
  - Show: `demos/research-report-app/app.py`.
  - Run: `uv run python -m course access` → `make backend` → `make app`.
  - Ask learners: Run the app as one user, produce a brief, follow up, and download it. Start a second user's session and attempt to read the first session through the backend; expect denial.
  - Check: Demonstrate evidence, one real tool call, a follow-up turn, a handled failure, and passing evaluation results; explain your runtime choice and which checks were live.
  - Fallback: The app defaults to offline and can demonstrate authentication, session ownership, streaming progress, downloads, and mock approval without an API call.

## If an API call fails

- No HTTP response / DNS / timeout: diagnose the network path first. Do not label it a quota or key failure.
- 401 / invalid_api_key: the request is not authenticated; fix the server's key configuration without printing it.
- 429 / insufficient_quota: check [billing](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing) or [spend limits](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/limits). This is different from a transient rate limit.
- 429 / rate_limit_exceeded: pace requests, reduce concurrency, and retry with backoff.
- 403 / model_not_found / project mismatch: inspect model, organization, project, and key scope.
- Keep class moving with `uv run python -m course replay` or the offline runtime. See [error codes](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/error-codes).

## Close

- Collect the five-part exit demonstration and a one-sentence runtime choice.
- Run `uv run python -m course cleanup`; close app sessions and stop the local servers.
- Point learners to `optional/` only after the core path is complete.
